preregistration.acquisition_start_criterion: acquisition starts when the first schema-valid A4 replica observation or DAO schema snapshot is retained for inspection

a3_calibration_bundle.use_limit: EXP-0051 and the retained A3 bundle are calibration and design input only. They are never A4 evidence and cannot satisfy an A4 derivation, holdout, predicate, or independent-validation result.

origin_disclosure.prediction_not_rediscovery_disclosure: A3 observed moving row-directory starts, complete type-0/type-1 row prefixes, tag-05 reference pages, and the slot-relative 16,352-bit candidate before this plan. A4 tests frozen row-anchored predictions on three fresh replicas; it does not claim rediscovery from A3.

executed_reference_harness.role: design input only: a plan-driven reference evaluator built by a different agent against review-pass-4 normative rules; it is not the production analyzer, not the dispatch-gate transcript, and never A4 evidence
executed_reference_harness.ambiguity_resolution: every plan ambiguity it recorded (AMB-01..AMB-17) is resolved by a stated decision in harness_ambiguity_resolutions and in the normative text those decisions cite

preregistration.amendment_rule: while this unmerged base plan is under review it is edited in place and re-pinned; after merge and before acquisition every amendment is an additive hash-pinned revision, and after acquisition starts any change requires a new experiment id, plan file, and provenance entry

implementation_rebinding.source_rule: reuse A3 replica, checkpoint capture, content-addressed store, freeze/holdout, resume, manifest, and independent-validation machinery; replace the scientific analyzer and schema-lifecycle worker behavior with this A4 plan only
implementation_rebinding.worker_fail_closed_rule: before provider preflight, database creation, or artifact staging, parse the selected plan and reject unless its experiment id and path exactly match A4; every emitted document carries the exact experiment id, base plan SHA-256, and governing revision plan SHA-256

revision_binding_rule.base_rule: until an additive revision exists, plan_sha256 and revision_plan_sha256 both equal the SHA-256 of this base plan as pinned in README, EXP-0052, worker, analyzer, producer validator, and independent validator; schemas never contain that hash as a const
revision_binding_rule.future_revision_rule: the highest-numbered additive revision recorded before acquisition becomes governing; every evidence document carries its hash while plan_sha256 remains the base hash, and the closed bundle inventories the byte-exact base plus every governing revision in order
revision_binding_rule.tamper_rule: producer and independent validators reject any absent, altered, uninventoried, or hash-mismatched plan/revision file or binding field

implementation_rebinding.workflow_fail_closed_rule: contract, matrix, fan-in, validation, and upload reject non-A4 ids, missing plan/revision bindings, wrong code page, or a holdout opened before the derivation freeze

environment_binding.ansi_code_page_rule: GetACP must equal 1252 before database creation for DAO capture. The scientific encoding comparison separately registers strict Windows-1252 (C9 for U+00C9) and UTF-8 (C3 89); neither is used to locate catalog records.

question: Can table-relative row-directory locators, complete allocation-map rows, indirect extended-map traversal, and a minimum catalog field model derived from two fresh Jet 3 databases predict a role-rotated third holdout without refitting?

replicas.acquisition_independence: each replica is created, mutated, closed, schema-snapshotted, physically captured, validated, and uploaded by a separate matrix job with no shared database, page store, output directory, or mutable state
replicas.fan_in_rule: Evaluation has two phases. Derivation phase: using replicas 1 and 2 only, evaluate every non-holdout predicate for H1, H2, H3, and H4 in dependency order. A downstream derivation layer depends on the previous layer's unique derivation model, never on its holdout result. Canonically serialize and hash all four derivation results, then irreversibly close the derivation inputs and analyzer state. Holdout phase: only after that hash exists, acquire and structurally validate replica 3 and evaluate, without refit, H1 holdout, H2 holdout, H3 holdout, H4 root holdout, and H4 field holdout in that order. An upstream holdout failure makes downstream holdout predicates not_applicable; it does not alter any frozen candidate, derivation count, or derivation terminal.
replicas.environment_identity_rule: provider identity, architecture, PowerShell major, and Windows ANSI code page match exactly across replicas; recorded OS and Python patch may differ only within the bindings

identifier_discriminator.constraint: this is the only non-ASCII table, field, or index identifier
identifier_discriminator.name_capture_rule: The DAO snapshot validates only the logical BSTR code units and produces both expected byte candidates: strict Windows-1252 and UTF-8. It does not compare either candidate to physical bytes and cannot terminate A4-SCHEMA-SNAPSHOT because of a physical encoding mismatch. Physical comparison occurs only at H4 encoding evaluation. Read each DAO Name as a BSTR and record its exact UTF-16 code-unit sequence. Convert that sequence both with WideCharToMultiByte(1252, WC_NO_BEST_FIT_CHARS, ...), requiring usedDefaultChar == FALSE, and with strict UTF-8; record both lowercase output hex values with no Unicode normalization, case folding, best-fit mapping, or replacement.

tables.schema_operation_rule: exactly one listed logical schema operation occurs between closed checkpoints; a TableDefs.Append may append a preconfigured TableDef with its declared fields, but no second TableDefs, Fields, or Indexes collection mutation occurs in that transition. Every canonical transition comparison asserts that only the listed logical mutation occurred and all unrelated table, field, index, and index-field tuples are byte-identical.

row_algorithm.id: positive one-based monotonically increasing signed 32-bit integer per logical role; deleted T1 ids are reinserted unchanged
row_algorithm.payload: repeat ASCII A4|<role>|<Id as ten zero-padded decimal digits>| and truncate to exactly 240 characters
row_algorithm.rolling_sha256: one SHA-256 stream over Id signed little-endian u32, Payload UTF-8 length u16 little-endian, then ASCII Payload bytes
row_algorithm.reread_requirement: at every checkpoint, canonical snapshot row counts and rolling hashes equal the expected values for every extant table

dao_protocol.database_creation: Acquire workspace = DAO.DBEngine.36.Workspaces(0) once per database operation and invoke workspace.CreateDatabase(path, dbLangGeneral, dbVersion30). dbLangGeneral is ;LANGID=0x0409;CP=1252;COUNTRY=0 and dbVersion30 is numeric 32. Any different receiver is a protocol failure.
dao_protocol.object_construction: Construct every TableDef, Field, and Index with the named DAO CreateTableDef, CreateField, or CreateIndex method. Before append set every scheduled TableDef Attributes = 0; set Id.Attributes = 0, Id Required=False, and record AllowZeroLength=null as not applicable; set Payload.Attributes = dbFixedField and require numeric value 1, Payload Required=False, and AllowZeroLength=False; set index Primary=False, Unique=False, Required=False, IgnoreNulls=False and set the sole index field Descending = False. Require every schema snapshot value to equal these construction constants at every applicable checkpoint.
dao_protocol.recordset_protocol: Open one dynaset per insertion/deletion leg with dbOpenDynaset numeric 2 and options numeric 0. For insertion use AddNew, assign Id and Payload, then Update once per row in ascending Id order. For deletion enumerate Id ascending and call Delete once per row.
dao_protocol.transaction_policy: No DAO workspace BeginTrans, CommitTrans, or rollback call is used; every AddNew/Update and Delete autocommits under DAO's default policy.
dao_protocol.measurement_loop: After every fixed 32-row batch, close Recordset, Database, and DBEngine references, poll size and SHA-256 every 250 milliseconds until three consecutive equal observations or 30 seconds, read the closed file page count, and either capture the threshold checkpoint or reopen and continue.
dao_protocol.row_cap_rule: Before a batch that would exceed 200000 inserted rows, terminate A4-RESOURCE-BOUND without executing a partial batch.
dao_protocol.churn_rule: T1_DELETE_ALL and T1_REINSERT_SAME use the same absent-transaction policy and ascending Id order. No compact or repair operation occurs.
dao_protocol.error_rule: Any DAO call failure closes all live references, retains diagnostics outside the successful artifact name, and creates no schema-valid evidence manifest.
dao_protocol.read_only_reopen: After close, reopen with exactly workspace.OpenDatabase(path, False, True, ""); False is exclusive and True is read-only. Any different receiver or argument tuple is a protocol failure.
dao_protocol.ordinal_filtering: After TableDefs.Refresh, snapshot user tables are exactly the extant scheduled physical names from expected_schema_by_checkpoint; snapshot user indexes are exactly the extant scheduled name A4IX_ID. Any extra or missing scheduled object fails A4-SCHEMA-SNAPSHOT; no implementation-defined hidden/system index test is used. Fields and index fields are all members after Refresh. Assign zero-based ordinals only after each exact declared filter and reject duplicate ordinals or names.

checkpoint_design.d_growth_rule: legacy machinery field: T1 relative growth uses fixed 32-row batches and the immediately preceding closed-file baseline named by the schedule; capture the first state meeting each threshold and disclose overshoot
checkpoint_design.d_regrowth_rule: legacy machinery field: T2 drop/recreate uses the exact same physical identifier and definition but assumes no page, identifier, or byte reuse; capture both closed states
checkpoint_design.relative_growth_rule: Capture T1 baseline once from actual_file_pages(T4_CREATE) after that checkpoint is closed and before the first T1 batch. Capture T4 baseline once from actual_file_pages(T3_ABS_16480) after that checkpoint is closed and before the first T4 batch. Relative threshold is baseline plus the decimal suffix; overshoot is achieved minus threshold.
checkpoint_design.absolute_growth_rule: For every T3 absolute checkpoint, target_baseline_pages is null, threshold is the decimal suffix, and overshoot is achieved minus threshold.
checkpoint_design.schedule_minimization_basis: the user-approved brief freezes exactly 25 checkpoints. Schema mutations isolate table creation, field append, index append, and T2 lifecycle; growth, churn, and idle legs reuse A3-equivalent thresholds without adaptive additions or retuning

page_capture.checkpoint_representation: ordered physical-page SHA-256 values from page zero through the final page
page_capture.dao_schema_snapshot_rule: after closing and before physical capture, reopen read-only through DAO, emit one canonical schema snapshot document, close again, assert the MDB hash is unchanged by the read-only observation, then capture physical pages
page_capture.schema_snapshot_comparison_rule: A4-SCHEMA-SNAPSHOT fails iff any of the 75 snapshots is missing, schema-invalid, mapped to the wrong replica/checkpoint/role binding, violates the exact scheduled extant schema, construction constants, row count/hash, code page, logical BSTR-to-expected-byte conversions, or before/after hash equality. It never compares an expected encoding candidate with physical bytes. Each transition must contain only its listed logical mutation; every unrelated canonical table, field, index, and index-field tuple remains byte-identical.
page_capture.snapshot_cross_binding_rule: For each checkpoint, the producer and independent validator load the referenced snapshot and require equality of experiment, plan, revision, commit, campaign, environment, provider, replica, checkpoint id, and ordinal. Require snapshot database_sha256_before_read == database_sha256_after_read == page_index.database_sha256, and require the manifest entry's path/hash/size to equal the observation reference and actual bytes.

record_candidate_procedure.row_directory_source: SRC-0020: tag-01 data page; u16 little-endian row count at bytes [8,10); row-offset entries at [10+2*i,12+2*i); evaluate both offset masks 0x1fff and 0x0fff as frozen nuisance candidates; 0x8000 deleted and 0x4000 overflow flags are explicit
record_candidate_procedure.row_boundary_rule: for slot i, start = raw_offset & mask; end = 2048 for slot 0, otherwise the preceding slot start. H1 consumes only page existence, tag 01, target uniqueness, and row ordinal < row_count. H2 then requires 10+2*row_count <= start < end <= 2048, nonoverlap in directory order, complete in-page bounds, and evaluates deleted/overflow flags. Moving starts across checkpoints are permitted and expected.
record_candidate_procedure.locator_enumeration: Raw syntactically decodable four-byte windows are enumeration work, not scientific candidates. H1 applies only the preregistered byte-level table-record signature independent of locator layout, two distinct nonoverlapping intervals in canonical offset order, offset identity across all applicable derivation checkpoints, and target page/tag/row-ordinal validity. Apply candidate_grammars.h1.filter_order exactly. H1 never decodes allocation rows, tests polarity or transitions, or assigns roles. Layout and pair cardinality are computed only from the target-valid set after A4-H1-TARGET-ROW-INVALID passes.

map_row_layouts.type_0: For a type-0 row, byte 0 is tag 00, bytes [1,5) are a little-endian u32 base, and bytes [5,row_len) are an LSB-first bitmap. Bit index k refers to absolute page base + k. The registered polarity candidates are set_bit_owned_in_use and clear_bit_owned_in_use; H2 lifecycle legs select exactly one polarity/row-role model, and only bits classified owned/in-use admit pages.
map_row_layouts.type_1: For a type-1 row, byte 0 is tag 01 and bytes [1,row_len) must have length divisible by four; otherwise A4-H2-MAP-TAG-UNSUPPORTED fails. Slot ordinal is the zero-based u32 position after the tag. Zero is inactive. A nonzero slot is an exact physical tag-05 page reference. A tag-05 page has header [0,4) and an LSB-first bitmap [4,2048); bit index k maps by the registered base formula, and only set bits of the owned/in-use row admit pages.

record_candidate_procedure.qualified_page_rule: schema lifecycle deltas qualify at most 16 tag-02 pages for H1 and allocation-admitted traversal qualifies at most 16 tag-01 or tag-05 pages per later layer; hash-state absence is explicit and a page is charged once across the union of derivation replicas A qualified page identity is (page number, checkpoint id) in the derivation union (AMB-03).

union_once_charging.rule: row slots, locator pairs, references, bitmap bits, catalog rows, and candidate models are counted once per unique qualified page/checkpoint/model identity in the union across derivation replicas however many replicas expose it; replica agreement is a predicate, not a second work charge
union_once_charging.resource_units: charge one unit for each row-directory entry decoded, locator layout/offset pair tested, slot/reference decoded, bitmap bit inspected, catalog field candidate tested, and candidate transition evaluation
union_once_charging.exact_ceiling_rule: Bounds classified attainable_exact have equality/one-over fixtures. Conservative upper bounds are proved by inequalities and make no attainability claim; the work-unit ceiling is conservative and its comparator is tested by injection, not by a byte campaign. Fail-fast evaluation charges only work reached after prior predicates.

calibration_receipt.verification_rule: the focused contract decodes the receipt's retained byte slices, little-endian locators/slots/bases, row-directory masks, and tag-05 capacity arithmetic; prose substring matching is insufficient

row_directory_procedure.subject: each H1-located map row at its checkpoint-specific directory bounds
row_directory_procedure.candidate_source: the two SRC-0020 offset-mask projections only; no changed-byte, fill, or frozen absolute-offset candidate
row_directory_procedure.survival_rule: the same offset-mask model must yield valid complete rows and flags in both derivation replicas at every applicable checkpoint, while row start/end values may move
row_directory_procedure.ambiguity_rule: Directory validity and map tags are evaluated per registered row mask: a mask that yields an invalid complete directory or an unsupported tag for any located row at any applicable checkpoint is eliminated, A4-H2-ROW-DIRECTORY-INVALID fails iff no mask yields a valid complete directory, and A4-H2-MAP-TAG-UNSUPPORTED fails iff no surviving mask yields supported tags; deleted or overflow flags are read from the raw entry independent of mask and yield A4-H2-ROW-FLAGS-INVALID; multiple masks that produce byte-identical complete bounds for every located row are one canonical model, and surviving masks carry into the H2 role candidates as the row_mask dimension

candidate_grammars.closure_rule: Candidate grammars are closed. The analyzer and validators may enumerate only models listed in this plan. Every nuisance choice (TDEF lifecycle signature, locator ordering, row mask, type-0 polarity/base rule, role transition signature, type-1 suffix rule, slot ordinal, catalog-root selection signature, catalog kind/id/name field width, endianness, length rule, value mapping, and identifier lifecycle relation) is an explicit finite enum or bounded integer domain below. An absent grammar is a preregistration error that blocks acquisition; it is not filled in by implementation and is not a scientific no_outcome.
candidate_grammars.canonical_enumeration: Enumerate the cartesian products below lexicographically by the listed enum order and then ascending integer. Canonical candidates omit replica-specific physical names, sort tables by T1,T2,T3,T4, sort locator offsets ascending, and are byte-unique canonical JSON objects.
candidate_grammars.phase_specific_candidate_contract: Separate predicate_measured_survivor_count from final-layer model cardinality. Closed, stage-discriminated candidate schemas exist for every stage at which candidates actually exist: H1 TDEF, H1 target-valid layout, H1 locator pair; H2 final role model; H3 conversion and final base formula; H4 root, operation record, structural field, and final encoded field. There is no H2 structural-decoder stage: directory, flag, and tag invalidity occur before any H2 candidate survives and are retained as invalid-observation payloads. Every predicate contract declares counted_set_kind, terminal_payload_schema, and an optional candidate_stage. At a terminal, serialize and hash only the candidates that exist at that predicate's named input stage; never manufacture fields selected only by downstream predicates. terminal_payload_schema candidate_set stores exactly the counted set; grouped_candidate_set stores every complete operation-record candidate in seven ordered operation groups; replica_pair stores the two unequal per-replica models and an empty union candidate array; invalid_observation stores an input_model_id plus a bounded byte-derived observation and no fabricated downstream candidate. The frozen layer records its terminal payload kind, stage, and candidate schema; decisive results alone contain the final model type. The analysis report byte-for-byte reproduces all frozen stage arrays, terminal evidence, and hashes.

tdef_lifecycle_signature_rules.new_tag_02_at_role_create: For each listed lifecycle instance, the physical page is nonextant or not tag 02 immediately before its TableDefs.Append, becomes an extant tag-02 page immediately after, and remains tag 02 through that instance's last extant checkpoint. T2-v1 ceases to be an extant tag-02 candidate at T2_DROP; T2-v2 is selected independently at T2_RECREATE.
tdef_lifecycle_signature_rules.preexisting_tag_02_hash_transition: The same physical tag-02 page is extant on both sides of the instance's TableDefs.Append and its page hash changes across that transition. It is byte-identical across every unrelated schema transition and idle pair; changes during that role's later field/index or data mutations are allowed and recorded. T2 drop and recreate must each change the candidate, and T2-v1/v2 locator pairs are tracked as distinct lifecycle instances.

h1.layout_candidate_rule: Raw syntactically decodable four-byte windows are enumeration work, not scientific candidates. A window at offset o (0..2044) is syntactically decodable under a layout iff at every derivation checkpoint of that replica its u24 little-endian page value is <= 20479; the u8 row byte is unconstrained at this stage (AMB-01). LOCATOR-LAYOUT-NONE asks whether either layout has any such cross-checkpoint syntactically preserved window. Structural pair filtering then applies only the registered table-record signature with its exact locator holes, nonoverlap, and identity preservation, so each layout admits at most the one canonical pair (35,39). After TARGET-ROW-INVALID passes, a layout cardinality candidate is a layout containing at least one target-valid pair.

table_record_signature.mask_rule: Compare (page_byte & mask_byte) == (value_byte & mask_byte) for all 92 bytes. Mask 00 is permitted only at mutable bytes [12,14) and the two locator intervals [35,43); all other mask bytes are ff. The signature identifies a bounded table record and is independent of locator layout and decoded locator values.

h1.h1_semantic_boundary: H1 uses only TDEF lifecycle bytes, syntactic locator decoding, the masked record signature, nonoverlap/identity, and target page/tag/row-ordinal validity. It does not decode allocation rows, test bit polarity, compare admitted sets, or assign owned/available roles; all such transition work belongs exclusively to H2.
non_holdout_local_order: 3. LOCATOR-LAYOUT-NONE — neither layout has any cross-checkpoint syntactically preserved window
4. LOCATOR-PAIR-NONE — windows exist but no masked, nonoverlapping, identity-preserved pair exists under either layout
5. TARGET-ROW-INVALID — structural pairs exist but none has two distinct targets that are extant tag 01 with in-range row ordinals at every applicable checkpoint
6. LOCATOR-LAYOUT-MULTIPLE — target-valid pairs survive under more than one layout
7. LOCATOR-PAIR-MULTIPLE — more than one target-valid pair survives under the unique layout
h1.overlap_policy: Enumerate canonical offsets a<b. Reject b-a<4 before reading the second interval. Adjacent [a,a+4) and [b,b+4) intervals are allowed when b-a=4. Reject duplicate decoded (page,row) targets only at A4-H1-TARGET-ROW-INVALID, not during pair filtering.

a3_page_23_recomputed_work.target_observation: The signature matches 25/25 page-23 blobs. Under row-then-page, offsets 35/39 resolve page 24 rows 0/1; page 24 is extant tag 01 with row count 2 at 25/25 checkpoints. Under page-then-row, the same bytes resolve pages 6144/6145 row 0; those pages are absent at 18/25 checkpoints.
a3_page_23_recomputed_work.decodability_rule: u24 page <= 20479 at all 25 checkpoints; offsets 0..2044; row byte unconstrained (AMB-01)

transition_signature.idle: both decoded rows and admitted-page sets byte-identical
transition_signature.grow: on the growing role's leg its owned/in-use admitted set may gain pages and may not lose any; its available set may not gain any page the owned set gained on that leg; instances of other roles are unconstrained on that leg (AMB-07)
transition_signature.delete_all: owned/in-use admitted set may remove and available may add; neither may change outside the T1 allocation span
transition_signature.reinsert: owned/in-use admitted set may add and available may remove; neither may change outside the T1 allocation span
transition_signature.drop_recreate: the dropped T2 instance has no owned set after drop; recreated T2-v2 receives a separately traversed set and no equality with T2-v1 is assumed

h2.type_1_suffix_rule: reject unless row_len minus one is divisible by four
h2.slot_ordinal_rule: zero-based u32 position after the tag
h2.static_fit_rule: A role/polarity/mask candidate fits the static structure iff at every applicable checkpoint every type-0 admitted page lies below that checkpoint's page count, the available set is a subset of the owned/in-use set, and the owned/in-use set is nonempty at every checkpoint where the instance's snapshot row count is greater than zero. A type-1 row is tested at H2 only for tag and u32-multiple validity; H3 decodes its admitted set (AMB-05).
h2.locator_role_assignments_rule: ordinal 0 and ordinal 1 are the H1 locator ordinals in ascending offset order, replica-invariant under the H1 model; a replica in which the other located row is owned yields a different canonical H2 model (AMB-15)

h3.conversion_rule: H3 conversion candidates describe only the structural type-0-to-type-1/nonzero-slot transition. They do not assert the page tag or referenced-page validity. A4-H3-REFERENCE-INVALID exclusively validates that every required nonzero reference resolves in-range to tag 05. This separation applies to rules and fixtures.
h3.base_discrimination_rule: H3 input-region coverage requires exactly these six regions: an inactive (zero) slot, an active slot, bit 0 set in a referenced bitmap, a nonzero bit set, bit 16351 set in slot s, and bit 0 set in slot s+1 with both slots active. It does not require a referenced page distinct from the slot ordinal. BASE-NONE/MULTIPLE then count fitting formulas. The BASE-MULTIPLE fixture uses reference == slot for every observation, causing the slot-base and referenced-page-base formulas both to fit; the decisive fixture includes reference != slot and leaves exactly one (AMB-08).
h3.fit_rule: A base formula fits iff at every conversion leg the preceding type-0 owned set is contained in the formula-decoded type-1 set and every later leg obeys the H2 transition signatures on formula-decoded sets; no extant-page rule is applied to admitted pages (AMB-08).

catalog_root_selection_signature_rules.operation_delta_non_name_structure: A root candidate is a tag-02 page extant at EMPTY whose frozen H1 locator layout, H2 decoder/role model, and H3 traversal are valid at every checkpoint and whose admitted stream (admitted page set or admitted page hashes) changes at every one of the five TableDefs.Append operations (T1_CREATE_ID, T2_CREATE, T2_RECREATE, T3_CREATE, T4_CREATE); changes at T1_ADD_TEXT and T1_ADD_INDEX are recorded but not required for candidacy. The H1 user table-record signature is not applied to system TDEFs. Locate the root and one operation-delta record candidate per instance solely by listed-operation before/after deltas and complete row bounds; do not inspect name bytes or name-length fields while selecting the root or operation-delta records (AMB-09).

h4.system_tdef_source: tag-02 pages extant at EMPTY; apply the frozen H1 locator layout, H2 decoder/role model, and H3 traversal independently without refit
h4.catalog_record_source: After one root survives, SCHEMA-DELTA-OUTSIDE-OWNED compares every isolated physical schema delta with the root-admitted page set before record candidates are restricted to admitted pages. Only if every delta is inside are complete SRC-0020 record candidates restricted to allocation-admitted tag-01 pages.
h4.h4_ordering_rule: After one root survives, `SCHEMA-DELTA-OUTSIDE-OWNED` compares every isolated physical schema delta with the root-admitted page set before record candidates are restricted to admitted pages. Only if every delta is inside does `CATALOG-RECORD-NONE` require at least one record for each of the five required table operation instances, followed by `CATALOG-RECORD-MULTIPLE` requiring at most one per required instance; the two contrast operations are grouped and counted in the same payload but never tested. Field-model predicates follow. The OUTSIDE fixture keeps every admitted delta and adds one non-admitted, non-user page change and therefore first fails OUTSIDE.
h4.name_anchor: No name anchor is used for root or operation-delta record selection. After exactly one record per required table instance survives, the encoding-neutral union of both registered expected-name byte sequences locates deferred compatible occurrences for bounded structural field-layout enumeration; neither encoding is preferred. Encoding-class fitting is evaluated only after exactly one structural tuple survives.
h4.encoding_neutral_union_anchor: After one operation-delta record per required table instance survives (contrast records are scanned when present), scan each complete row for every exact occurrence of each registered expected-name byte sequence without preferring an encoding, deduplicating identical CP1252/UTF-8 byte sequences within that operation before the union scan. For every occurrence enumerate kind_start_delta 1..16, kind width 1/2/4, immediately preceding identifier width 1/2/4, one shared integer-field endianness little/big for kind, identifier, and stored name length, name-length start delta 1..16 before the occurrence, and name-length width 1/2/4. Deduplicate identical non-name field-address tuples before structural cardinality, retaining the compatible name occurrences per operation only as deferred encoding evidence. After one structural tuple survives, evaluate the compatible occurrences against the three encoding/length equivalence classes.
h4.union_anchor_occurrence_bound: A complete row has at most 2,036 bytes because a valid one-row page requires the ten-byte header and one two-byte row-directory entry. For each operation, deduplicate identical CP1252/UTF-8 expected byte sequences before the union scan. The maximum distinct-pattern scan is nine complete-row scans, 9*2036=18,324 byte-start charges. Compatible occurrences are charged per operation: each of five table operations contributes at most floor(2036/8)=254, and each of the Payload and A4IX_ID operations contributes at most floor(2036/7)=290, for a total of 1,850 occurrence identities.
h4.relative_field_delta_domain: kind_start_delta and name_length_start_delta are each 1..16 bytes before a compatible encoding-neutral name occurrence; kind, immediately preceding identifier, and name-length widths are each 1/2/4, with registered endianness choices.
h4.name_length_endianness_rule: exactly the candidate endianness; not an independent grammar dimension and not a candidate field. The sole endianness field governs kind, identifier, and stored name length.
h4.field_candidate_shapes: h4StructuralFieldCandidate contains only occurrence_evidence_sha256, the encoding-neutral kind/id/name-length deltas and widths, one shared registered endianness, the table kind value {table: value}, the identifier-lifecycle relation, and an exact seven-entry compatible_occurrences_by_operation array in checkpoint-operation order. Each entry holds the operation id, the compatible occurrence count (at least 1 for the five required operations, 0 or more for the two contrast operations), and a fixed-width LSB-first bitmap over that operation's occurrence indexes in the bound h4_occurrence_evidence table: 64 hex characters (256 bits, bits 254..255 zero) for the five eight-byte table operations and 74 hex characters (296 bits, bits 290..295 zero) for Payload and A4IX_ID; the bitmap popcount equals the count. No occurrence object, name_start, stored-length value, or encoding/length equivalence class is stored inside a structural candidate. h4FinalFieldCandidate contains one structural_candidate_id, exactly one registered encoding_length_equivalence_class, and an exact seven-entry selected_operation_occurrences array whose occurrence_index for each operation MUST have its bit set in the referenced structural candidate's bitmap for that operation. The global scalar name_start is forbidden. The candidate also records value_equivalent_tuple_count (1..27648): tuples decoding identical kind, identifier, and length values for every operation record at every applicable checkpoint are one model represented by the first tuple in canonical enumeration order (AMB-12).
h4.kind_value_mapping: The kind field is a 1/2/4-byte integer that decodes to one equal raw value across all five required table records at every applicable checkpoint; the candidate stores {table: value}. No field or index kind value is required: the raw kind value of a present contrast record and whether it differs from the table value are contrast observations only. Opaque bijection ids are forbidden.
h4.expected_kind_relations: T1_CREATE_ID, T2_CREATE, T2_RECREATE, T3_CREATE, and T4_CREATE records map to one equal table kind value. Contrast records, when present, are expected but not required to carry a kind value distinct from the table value; the observation is reported, never tested.
h4.identifier_oracle: No DAO physical identifier is claimed. Expected identity is the listed operation instance (T2-v1 differs from T2-v2); H4 predicts only equality/inequality of the physical candidate across those instances.
h4.expected_identifier_relations: The physical identifier candidate is stable for an operation instance across unrelated schema mutations, growth, churn, and idle checkpoints. T2-v1 and T2-v2 are required different only under stable_for_same_operation_instance_and_distinct_for_t2_v1_v2; they are required equal only under stable_for_same_physical_name_including_t2_v1_v2. All simultaneously extant object instances have distinct identifier values.
h4.expected_name_relations: Each located structural record is compared only at the encoding stage. Exact bytes must match one registered encoding with no normalization, folding, best-fit, or replacement; stored length must match one reported equivalence class. Table, field, and index names occur only for their extant listed operation instances. Contrast names are compared under the decisive class for reporting only.
h4.candidate_overflow_rule: canonical enumeration stops only after constructing candidate 4097; that event is A4-RESOURCE-BOUND and creates no scientific report or successful manifest

name_length_equivalence_classes.reason: For every strictly representable CP1252 identifier each scalar is exactly one byte, so no identifier within CP1252 can discriminate these members; report the class.

h4.encoding_length_evaluation_rule: After exactly one structural field-layout model survives, compare every compatible deferred occurrence of the five required records against exact strict Windows-1252 (C9 for U+00C9) and UTF-8 (C3 89) bytes and the selected stored length against the registered equivalence classes. Encoding failure records the actual fitting-class count. The zero-fit fixture contains no matching candidate; a multiple fixture, if registered, contains both registered byte occurrences at compatible deferred anchors and never claims two classes fit one É occurrence. The campaign contains no possible within-CP1252 discriminator because strict CP1252 is single-byte for every representable scalar; report cp1252_single_byte_per_scalar rather than selecting one observationally equivalent member.
h4.structural_raw_tuple: After one operation-delta record per each of the 5 required table instances survives: compatible name occurrences retained separately for every operation in the bound h4_occurrence_evidence table, kind_start_delta 1..16, kind_width 1/2/4, immediately preceding identifier_width 1/2/4, one shared kind/identifier/stored-name-length endianness little/big, name_length_start_delta 1..16, name_length_width 1/2/4, and one of 2 identifier lifecycle relations. The inner grammar is 16*3*3*2*16*3*2=27648; the kind test is equality across the five required records, so no kind permutation dimension exists. Encoding class remains deferred. Value-equivalent tuples (identical decoded kind/identifier/length values everywhere, including identical-address tuples) are one model before structural cardinality while the compatible occurrence subset of each operation is retained as a bitmap over the evidence table. Structural tests evaluate tuples against required-record occurrences only (at most 5*254=1,270 identities); contrast occurrences (at most 2*290=580) are evaluated once under the single surviving structural model.
h4.occurrence_evidence_table: After one operation-delta record per required table instance survives, the encoding-neutral union scan produces one canonical frozen h4_occurrence_evidence document (artifacts.h4_occurrence_evidence, schema h4-occurrence-evidence.schema.json) bound by SHA-256: the surviving root candidate id and exactly seven operation bindings in checkpoint-operation order (five required, two contrast whose locator is null and whose occurrence list is empty when no unique contrast record exists), each with the canonical record locator and its deduplicated raw name occurrences (occurrence_index, row-relative name_start, matched registered pattern id, matched bytes), at most 254 for each of the five table operations and 290 for Payload and A4IX_ID, 1,850 in total, canonical UTF-8 JSON at most 524,288 bytes. Every structural candidate references the table by hash instead of inlining occurrences, so a candidate stays under 4,096 bytes and the candidate-array proof closes. The independent validator recomputes every compatible length-field location and value from the bound page bytes and the evidence table, recomputes each bitmap, and verifies final-candidate occurrence membership. The evidence reference is null whenever structural enumeration never began.
h4.encoding_result_rule: H4 freezes two independent field results after root_result: structural_result and encoding_result. structural_result always retains the complete operation-record or h4StructuralFieldCandidate set and its hash once record or structural enumeration begins. encoding_result is not_applicable unless structural_result is a one-model result. FIELD-MODEL-MULTIPLE stores two or more structural candidates and no final candidates. ENCODING-AMBIGUOUS with zero or multiple fits retains exactly one structural candidate in structural_result and stores zero or at least two h4FinalFieldCandidate objects in encoding_result. Decisive H4 retains exactly one object in each result. Every final candidate's structural_candidate_id MUST equal the retained structural candidate's canonical_candidate_id, so all final candidates in an encoding-multiple set share one structural id and differ only by registered equivalence class and selected occurrences; for each required operation the selected occurrence index MUST be a member of the retained structural candidate's compatible bitmap. Reject an orphan structural id, a selected occurrence absent from the structural bitmap, duplicate equivalence classes, or any final candidate when structural cardinality is not exactly one. H4 REPLICA-DISAGREEMENT retains the per-replica structural pair in structural_result and the per-replica final pair in encoding_result; the final pair must be unequal, the structural pair may be equal. Contrast operations carry a nullable selected occurrence that is reported, never tested.
h4.isolated_delta_rule: At a listed operation transition the isolated physical schema delta is the set of changed page indices minus page 0 and page 1, every user instance's TDEF page, every user H1-located map page, and every page admitted by a user instance's frozen H2/H3 traversal at that checkpoint. Page 0 is excluded, not assumed static (AMB-10).
h4.length_plausibility_rule: Before deduplication, for every operation record and every compatible occurrence the stored length decoded under the tuple's width and endianness must equal one of the registered encoding-neutral counts for the expected name: strict Windows-1252 byte count, UTF-8 byte count, or Unicode scalar count (8, 9, 8 for A4TAB_É4; all equal for ASCII names). The test selects no class (AMB-11).
h4.table_operation_record_rule: Catalog-root record predicates require exactly one operation-delta record per TABLE lifecycle operation instance: the five TableDefs.Append operations T1_CREATE_ID, T2_CREATE, T2_RECREATE, T3_CREATE, and T4_CREATE. T2_DROP is not a record-producing operation: it is covered by the identifier-lifecycle and name-extant relations (the T2-v1 record ceases to be extant at T2_DROP and T2-v2 is a fresh instance at T2_RECREATE). H4 does not bet on field or index names appearing in the catalog root.
h4.contrast_rule: T1_ADD_TEXT (Payload) and T1_ADD_INDEX (A4IX_ID) are contrast operations. They are located by the same operation-delta rule, scanned with the same encoding-neutral union scan, and reported in h4_catalog_bootstrap.contrast_result as a non-failing sub-result: for each contrast operation, record_candidate_count (measured, never tested against 1), record_present, the complete record bytes if exactly one record is present, compatible_occurrence_count, the raw kind value and whether it differs from the table kind, the selected occurrence under the surviving structural model, and whether the exact name bytes and stored length fit the decisive encoding class. No contrast value can terminate the layer, change a survivor count, or alter a structural or final candidate id. contrast_result is not_applicable until record enumeration begins; contrast fields that depend on a unique structural model or a decisive encoding class are null until that stage exists. Contrast observations are descriptive_provider_observation_only and claim nothing about physical column or index definition layout.

operation_binding_cardinality.rule: operation bindings, occurrence-evidence bindings, compatible-occurrence bitmaps, operation groups, and selected occurrences keep the seven-entry checkpoint order; the five required entries obey the table-record predicates and the two contrast entries are optional (count or locator may be zero/null) and never counted

A4-H1.model: schema lifecycle deltas select one tag-02 TDEF per logical table and exactly two table-relative locators under one frozen layout; both resolve to extant tag-01 pages and valid row slots at every applicable checkpoint
A4-H1.no_outcome: no or multiple TDEFs; no syntactically preserved layout windows; no structural locator pair; no target-valid pair; multiple target-valid layouts or pairs; replica disagreement; holdout prediction failure

A4-H2.model: the two H1 rows independently decode as complete type-0/type-1 rows and exactly one transition model assigns owned/in-use versus available across grow, delete-all, reinsert, drop/recreate, and idle legs; row motion is allowed
A4-H2.no_outcome: invalid row directory or flags; unsupported tag; zero or multiple role assignments; unexplained transition; replica disagreement; holdout prediction failure

A4-H3.model: conditional on an H2 type-1 row, zero slots are inactive, every nonzero u32 is the exact tag-05 page reference, bitmap bytes are [4,2048), and absolute page = slot_ordinal * 16352 + bit_index; freeze every active/inactive slot and boundary flip before holdout
A4-H3.no_outcome: no conversion; no inactive-slot observation; invalid reference; insufficient base discrimination; zero or multiple base formulas; replica disagreement; holdout prediction failure

Field and index appends are a reported, non-failing contrast.
A4-H4.no_outcome: zero or multiple catalog roots, records, or field models; schema delta outside admitted pages; encoding ambiguity; replica disagreement; holdout root or field prediction failure
A4-H4.separate_reporting: catalog root/location, structural field-layout, and encoded-field results are reported independently as root_result, structural_result, and encoding_result so a field or encoding failure cannot erase root or structural success; contrast_result reports the T1_ADD_TEXT/T1_ADD_INDEX observations and can never terminate the layer

dry_run_honesty_clause.reachability_by_transcript: Before any hosted dispatch, an executed byte-level reachability harness must demonstrate every terminal classified claimed-reachable and assert every terminal classified unreachable. A registry label, constant rejection, hand-authored expected status, or structural unit test is not reachability evidence.

byte_level_reachability_harness_contract.shared_campaign: A reachability fixture contains one shared synthetic campaign: exact 2,048-byte page blobs, page indexes, checkpoint/lifecycle events, DAO snapshot values, and the expected mutation from the all-pass baseline. It MUST NOT contain `accepted` or `valid` verdict booleans. The evaluator decodes the fixture bytes, enumerates only ids/tuples present in the registered grammar, applies filters in the normative order, propagates each surviving candidate set to the next predicate, and then reports the first failure. A fixture is accepted only if every earlier predicate passes on that same state and the target predicate is its first failure.
byte_level_reachability_harness_contract.survivor_count_handling: `exact: n` requires measured count `== n`; `minimum: n` requires measured count `>= n` and stores the actual measured count. `exactly_one_accepted` returns the actual fitting cardinality on both pass and failure. A predicate whose failure permits both zero and multiple candidates declares `allowed_ranges: [{"exact": 0}, {"minimum": 2}]`; it never substitutes the structural-model count 1 for the encoding-candidate count.
byte_level_reachability_harness_contract.required_adversarial_cases: The transcript's adversarial_case_outcomes is an exact keyed object with ten fixed cases and fixed expectations: multiple_count_2, multiple_count_3, multiple_count_4, encoding_count_0, and encoding_count_2 expect acceptance as legitimate measured outcomes; unregistered_candidate_id, malformed_page, earlier_predicate_invalidated (a target mutation that also invalidates an earlier predicate), and resource_one_over (the byte-level 67,200-changed-entry campaign of the A4-RESOURCE-BOUND fixture) expect rejection; work_counter_comparator_equality injects a measured work counter of exactly 600,000,000 into the checked comparator and expects acceptance, and is a comparator test outside the 40 byte-level fixtures. A duplicate, missing, or renamed case, or a result differing from its fixed expectation, is rejected.
byte_level_reachability_harness_contract.enumeration_and_reporting: The harness uses grammar-only enumeration, the normative filter order, shared propagated state, first-failure reporting, and measured survivor counts with exact, minimum, and allowed_ranges semantics. It emits the actual count for every evaluated predicate and rejects an unregistered id or tuple before scientific filtering.
byte_level_reachability_harness_contract.dispatch_gate: The harness and transcript must be executed, retained, hash-bound, and disclosed additively before any hosted dispatch. Every claimed-reachable terminal must be the measured first failure of its byte fixture; every unreachable terminal must be explicitly asserted unreachable by enumeration.

predicate_registry.evaluation_rule: Evaluation has two phases. Derivation phase: using replicas 1 and 2 only, evaluate every non-holdout predicate for H1, H2, H3, and H4 in dependency order. A downstream derivation layer depends on the previous layer's unique derivation model, never on its holdout result. Canonically serialize and hash all four derivation results, then irreversibly close the derivation inputs and analyzer state. Holdout phase: only after that hash exists, acquire and structurally validate replica 3 and evaluate, without refit, H1 holdout, H2 holdout, H3 holdout, H4 root holdout, and H4 field holdout in that order. An upstream holdout failure makes downstream holdout predicates not_applicable; it does not alter any frozen candidate, derivation count, or derivation terminal. Evaluate campaign predicates first in registered order. For an applicable predicate, pass means and only means its registered pass_iff condition is true; otherwise record fail, use that predicate id as the sole terminal for its scope, and mark every later predicate in that scope not_applicable. After a campaign failure, all 36 scientific predicates are not_applicable and no successful evidence bundle is created. A decisive derivation layer has every derivation predicate pass, terminal id null, survivor count 1, and one frozen candidate. No predicate may infer semantics from its id. Each terminal records its contract's terminal_payload_schema: candidate_set (the counted set), grouped_candidate_set (seven ordered operation groups), replica_pair (two unequal per-replica models), or invalid_observation (an input model reference plus a bounded byte-derived observation). A layer result whose terminal payload is not candidate_set may have a candidate array length that differs from predicate_measured_survivor_count; the count is validated against the declared counted set. A4-RESOURCE-BOUND is evaluated fourth over the campaign-level resources and stays armed: a later attempt to construct candidate 4,097, occurrence identity 1,851, an over-bound JSON document, or (by comparator unit test only) work unit 600,000,001 during layer evaluation is the same terminal, aborts evaluation, and creates no scientific report or successful manifest. Its registered byte-level reachability fixture is campaign-level so that its transcript entry has the exact four-predicate prefix. Cardinality and validity predicates are evaluated on replica 1 and then replica 2; the first violating replica supplies the measured count and the retained candidates (AMB-04). Campaign predicates run per replica as each replica is structurally validated: replicas 1 and 2 before derivation and replica 3 only after the frozen-document hash exists and before any holdout predicate; the report's campaign rows are the conjunction over all three replicas (AMB-13).

For a terminal result: candidate_set requires candidate array length == predicate_measured_survivor_count; grouped_candidate_set requires every group cardinality == its candidate_ids length, the union of groups == the candidate array, and predicate_measured_survivor_count == the minimum group cardinality for RECORD-NONE and the maximum group cardinality (>= 2) for RECORD-MULTIPLE; replica_pair requires an empty candidate array, two entries in replica order with recomputed ids, unequal canonical models, and predicate_measured_survivor_count == 2; invalid_observation requires input_model_id to reference the decisive upstream candidate (empty candidate array) or the single same-layer input candidate retained in the array, and predicate_measured_survivor_count == 1.

decision_rules.freeze_rule: Using replicas 1 and 2 only, evaluate every non-holdout predicate through H4, canonically serialize all four derivation results and transcripts, hash the frozen document, then irreversibly close derivation inputs and analyzer state before replica 3 is acquired or opened.
decision_rules.holdout_rule: After the frozen-document SHA-256 exists, acquire and structurally validate replica 3 and evaluate H1, H2, H3, H4 root, and H4 fields in that order without refit. Upstream holdout failure gates later holdouts but never changes frozen bytes, candidates, counts, or derivation terminals. Replica 3's campaign predicates are evaluated only after that hash exists (AMB-13).

survivor_count_reconciliation.rule: The 40 predicate_contracts are the normative count table. exact: n requires predicate_measured_survivor_count == n; minimum: n requires predicate_measured_survivor_count >= n and stores the actual measured count; allowed_ranges accepts only a listed exact or minimum range and stores the actual measured count; per_replica_exact 1 / replica_count 2 / total_exact 2 requires a replica pair and measured count 2. At a derivation terminal the frozen result stores the payload declared by terminal_payload_schema (predicate_registry.terminal_payload_rule) and derivation_survivor_count is zero because no final-layer model exists. A decisive model stores one final-stage candidate, predicate_measured_survivor_count 1, derivation_survivor_count 1, and no terminal payload. not_applicable stores both counts zero, an empty set, and no terminal payload. Holdout failures are reported separately and do not change the one-model frozen set. Campaign failures count 0.

decision_rules.replica_agreement_rule: replica 1 and 2 must each independently yield one canonically equivalent logical-role model; physical page numbers, row slots, and identifiers may rotate only where the frozen model declares the mapping
decision_rules.no_outcome_projection: Report derivation status and holdout status separately. A downstream derivation layer depends only on the previous unique derivation model; a downstream holdout depends on the preceding holdout. Campaign failure prevents all scientific evaluation and yields no successful evidence bundle.
decision_rules.frozen_set_shape_rule: A frozen layer contains only its derivation status (model | no_outcome | not_applicable), derivation terminal if any, terminal_payload_kind, terminal_candidate_stage, predicate_measured_survivor_count, final-layer derivation_survivor_count, the complete stage-discriminated canonical candidates that exist at that stage, terminal_evidence (replica pair, operation groups, or invalid observation) where the contract declares it, instance bindings where registered, and candidates SHA-256. Decisive results alone contain the final model type. It MUST NOT contain holdout_evaluated, a holdout terminal, a holdout status, or any value computed from replica 3. H4 is frozen as root_result, structural_result, and encoding_result under candidate_grammars.h4.encoding_result_rule, with the frozen h4_occurrence_evidence reference (path, SHA-256, size) that every structural candidate's occurrence_evidence_sha256 must equal. H4 holdout reuses the frozen structural id, evidence table, per-operation bitmap rules, and final equivalence class without refit. The final analysis report separately records holdout predicates and outcomes and MUST require derivation_candidate_set_sha256, equal to the actual SHA-256 of the complete frozen file bytes, not a layers-only projection. Its candidate arrays, terminal evidence, evidence reference, instance bindings, transcripts, charges, and per-layer derivation fields MUST byte-for-byte equal the frozen values for decisive, NONE, MULTIPLE, derivation-invalid, and holdout-failure outcomes. The H4 contrast_result is a non-failing reported observation with its own measured counts; it is not a result slot, has no terminal, and carries no candidates.
decision_rules.h1_frozen_model_rule: The canonical H1 scientific model contains only replica-invariant fields: layout, masked table-signature id, and ascending table-relative locator offsets. A separate frozen instance_bindings array contains exactly T1-v1, T2-v1, T2-v2, T3-v1, and T4-v1 for each derivation replica, each with logical role, lifecycle instance, TDEF page, two locator targets (page 0..20479, row 0..255), and its exact inclusive applicable checkpoint range. The required ranges are T1-v1 T1_CREATE_ID..T4_IDLE_R; T2-v1 T2_CREATE..T2_CREATE; T2-v2 T2_RECREATE..T4_IDLE_R; T3-v1 T3_CREATE..T4_IDLE_R; T4-v1 T4_CREATE..T4_IDLE_R. logical_role equals the lifecycle prefix, start is not after end in checkpoint order, and no binding may extend outside its lifecycle. Canonical replica agreement compares the invariant model and normalized logical-role behavior, not raw rotating page numbers. Holdout re-derives replica-3 bindings and tests the unchanged invariant model.
decision_rules.canonicalization_and_uniqueness_rule: For H1 recompute canonical_model_id as SHA256(canonical_json({model_type, model})) for replica-invariant scientific comparison and canonical_candidate_id as SHA256(canonical_json({model_type, model, instance_bindings})) for storage, sorting, and uniqueness. Distinct physical bindings may share a model id but must have distinct candidate ids. For other candidate stages recompute canonical_candidate_id from their complete registered identity. A decisive H1 candidate carries exactly the ten replica-1 and replica-2 bindings in canonical order; a terminal candidate-set H1 candidate carries exactly the five bindings of the replica on which the predicate failed (AMB-04); a replica-pair entry's complete H1 candidate carries exactly the five bindings of its own replica. Recompute the h4_occurrence_evidence SHA-256 from the retained file bytes and require every structural candidate's occurrence_evidence_sha256 and every bitmap popcount to agree with it. Require equality, ascending locator offsets, unique targets, canonical binding order, exact role/lifecycle coverage and ranges, and no duplicate page/row pair. Recompute each candidate-array hash and the actual complete frozen-file SHA-256. Canonicalize snapshot tables by declared DAO ordinal then strict CP-1252 name bytes; canonicalize fields/indexes/index fields by their declared DAO ordinal then name bytes. Independently reject duplicate logical roles, names, ordinals, predicate ids, and tamper ids. uniqueItems on whole JSON objects does not satisfy these uniqueness rules.
decision_rules.schema_semantic_validation_rule: Use a layer- and terminal-stage-discriminated union: H1 TDEF, target-valid layout, and locator-pair candidates; H2 final-role candidates; H3 conversion and final-base candidates; and H4 root, operation-record, structural-field, and final-encoded-field candidates all have closed required fields with additionalProperties false, and every terminal_evidence payload has a closed schema. Project layer status, terminal, terminal payload kind, terminal candidate stage, measured predicate count, final-layer count, H4 result-slot states, and downstream not_applicable state from predicate rows and the predicate contracts, and reject any mismatch. The analysis report must byte-for-byte reproduce every frozen stage array, terminal evidence, evidence reference, and hash. Project the five holdout_results entries exactly from predicate rows 36–40 and prerequisite gating. Then derive scientific_outcome from that validated projection. A derivation or holdout result may never disagree with its predicate row. Independently recompute total_work_units from the serialized term values and reject any mismatch. Validate transcript objects with concrete, bounded schemas rather than unconstrained objects.

work_model.candidate_json_closure: Enforce one global fail-fast maximum of 4,096 retained candidates across H1, H2, H3, H4 root, H4 structural, and H4 encoding. Each layer-discriminated candidate has canonical UTF-8 JSON length <=4096 bytes; the largest registered shapes are a ten-binding H1 locator-pair candidate and a structural field candidate with seven full-width bitmaps, both far below 4,096 because occurrence objects live only in the separate h4_occurrence_evidence document. Across all arrays, at most 4096 candidates plus brackets and separators give <=4096*4096+4097=16781313 bytes. Terminal evidence is bounded separately: a replica pair holds two candidates (<=8192 bytes plus fixed fields), operation groups hold at most 4096 candidate ids (<=4096*67+1024 bytes), and an invalid observation is <=1024 bytes; charge 300,000 bytes for all terminal evidence. The h4_occurrence_evidence document is at most 524,288 bytes and is counted exactly once. Concrete transcript maxima are row_directories 1024*512, locators 1024*384, map_transitions 1024*512, reference_bitmaps 1024*512, catalog_roots 1024*384, catalog_fields 4096*512: at most 4456448 encoded item bytes plus bounded separators. Candidate arrays, terminal evidence, the evidence document, transcripts, fixed fields, and 1 MiB envelope overhead total <23200000 bytes, below max_json_bytes=67108864. Reject candidate 4,097, candidate byte 4,097, occurrence identity 1,851, evidence byte 524,289, and report byte 67,108,865 before manifest creation. The report validator rejects downstream candidates after an upstream terminal before applying this JSON proof.
work_model.resource_class_rule: Each resource field is classified as either (a) attainable_exact, with an accepted fixture at exactly the bound and an otherwise identical one-over rejection, or (b) conservative_upper, with proof by inequalities but no claim of attainability. The sum of independent maxima is not an exact attainable ceiling. Fail-fast evaluation charges only work reachable after preceding predicates. Per-page row count and row length are jointly constrained; a valid page with one-byte rows satisfies 10+3n<=2048 and has at most 679 rows.
work_model.capacity_maxima: Type-1 complete u32 slots per maximum tag-01 row: 508. Type-0 bitmap capacity per maximum tag-01 row: 16,248 bits. Tag-05 bitmap capacity: 16,352 bits.

logical_read_consumers.rule: There is one full producer pass: 25*20480*2048 = 1048576000. The analyzer and independent validator each read at most every retained unique page blob once: 65536*2048 = 134217728 each. Total logical reads per replica are therefore at most 1048576000 + 2*134217728 = 1317011456, below 2 GiB. Each consumer records its own subtotal; the validator recomputes all three and their sum. No analyzer/validator pass is shared.

terminal_path_maxima.proof: Every maximum is recomputed by summing the named identities in terminal_path_maxima.term_table from work_model.terms, except the explicitly named invalid_path_row_directory_entries alternative, which is mutually exclusive with the valid path and all later terms. A complete row is at most 2,036 bytes. The nine deduplicated pattern/operation scans charge 18,324 starts; the five eight-byte table operations plus two seven-byte field/index operations charge 1,850 occurrence identities; one shared integer-field endianness gives inner grammar 27,648 and tuple term 35,112,960. The latest H4 path is 115,687,821. Every terminal path is <= max_analysis_work_units=600000000, and no registered path can charge the remaining 484,312,179 identities, so the bound is conservative_upper. The checked counter comparator accepts a unit-test measured-total argument of exactly 600,000,000 and rejects 600,000,001 before manifest creation; that comparator test is not a byte-level fixture.

work_model.attainable_exact_rule: For each attainable_exact field, accept equality and reject an otherwise identical one-over before manifest creation. Conservative_upper fields are independently recomputed and rejected only when exceeded; no equality fixture or attainability claim is made. max_analysis_work_units is conservative_upper: its equality/one-over tests exercise only the checked comparator (analyzer_dry_run_contract.dry_run_honesty_clause.work_counter_comparator_rule).

harness_ambiguity_resolutions.rule: Each recorded ambiguity has exactly one stated decision that is also written into the cited normative text; the analyzer and independent validator implement the decision, never the harness reading, where the two differ.

resolutions.decision: A four-byte window is syntactically decodable at an offset iff, at every derivation checkpoint of that replica, its u24 little-endian page value is <= 20479 (max_final_pages_per_replica - 1); the u8 row byte is unconstrained at this stage and the 2,045 offsets 0..2044 are examined per layout. This frozen page bound, not 65535 and not the per-checkpoint extant page count, is the decodability rule. The focused contract recomputes 1,872 preserved windows per layout on retained A3 page 23 under exactly this rule (<= 65535 gives 1,875 and the extant-page bound gives 1,855), so the recorded count stands.

The exact locator holes [35,39) and [39,43) admit at most one canonical pair (35,39) per layout, so A4-H1-LOCATOR-PAIR-MULTIPLE is unreachable_by_construction. It stays registered and ordered (it always passes when reached) so the count table and holdout gating are unchanged; its contract carries the enumeration proof, and the transcript schema fixes its entry to a null first failure with a mandatory unreachable assertion (max measured count 1 across the sweep).

A qualified page identity is (page number, checkpoint id) within the derivation union; a page number exposed by both derivation replicas at the same checkpoint is charged once. Role rotation does not change the identity rule.

Every NONE/MULTIPLE/invalid predicate is evaluated independently on replica 1 and then replica 2 in that order; it fails on the first replica violating it and stores that replica's measured count and that replica's candidates (H1 candidates then carry only that replica's five bindings). REPLICA-DISAGREEMENT compares the two replica-invariant canonical models and retains the unequal pair. A decisive candidate merges both replicas' bindings in canonical order.

A role/polarity/mask candidate fits the static structure iff at every applicable checkpoint every type-0 admitted page lies below that checkpoint's page count, the available set is a subset of the owned/in-use set, and the owned/in-use set is nonempty at every checkpoint where the instance's snapshot row count is greater than zero. A type-1 row is tested at H2 only for tag and u32-multiple validity; its admitted set is decoded by H3.

Idle legs are idle pairs already enforced byte-identical by A4-IDLE-EQUALITY, so the R19 fixture uses a grow-leg violation: during T1_REL_0512 the owned/in-use set of the unique role model loses a page.

On a role's grow leg that role's owned/in-use set may gain pages and may not lose any; its available set may not gain any page the owned set gained on that leg; instances of other roles are unconstrained on that leg.

resolutions.topic: H3 formula fit and input regions
resolutions.decision: A base formula fits iff at every conversion leg the preceding type-0 owned set is contained in the formula-decoded type-1 set and every later leg obeys the H2 transition signatures on formula-decoded sets; no extant-page rule is applied to admitted pages because exact_allocation_set_equality is not claimed. The six required input regions are: an inactive (zero) slot, an active slot, bit 0 set in a referenced bitmap, a nonzero bit set, bit 16351 set in slot s, and bit 0 set in slot s+1 with both slots active.

A catalog-root candidate is a tag-02 page extant at EMPTY whose frozen H1/H2/H3 traversal is valid at every checkpoint and whose admitted stream (admitted page set or admitted page hashes) changes at every one of the five TableDefs.Append operations; changes at T1_ADD_TEXT and T1_ADD_INDEX are recorded but not required for candidacy. The H1 user table-record signature is not applied to system TDEFs. OUTSIDE remains reachable because a listed operation may change an admitted page and an additional non-admitted page.

At a listed operation transition the isolated physical schema delta is the set of changed page indices minus page 0 and page 1 (file header and global allocation pages per SRC-0020, about which H4 claims nothing), every user instance's TDEF page, every user H1-located map page, and every page admitted by a user instance's frozen H2/H3 traversal at that checkpoint. Page 0 is not assumed static; it is excluded.

The structural stage tests stored-length plausibility before deduplication: for every operation record and every compatible occurrence, the stored length decoded under the tuple's width and endianness must equal one of the registered encoding-neutral counts for the expected name, namely its strict Windows-1252 byte count, its UTF-8 byte count, or its Unicode scalar count (8, 9, or 8 for A4TAB_É4; all equal for ASCII names). The test selects no class.

Tuples that decode identical kind, identifier, and stored-length values for every operation record at every applicable checkpoint are one canonical model whose representative is the first tuple in canonical enumeration order; the candidate records value_equivalent_tuple_count. Identical-address deduplication is the special case of this rule.

Campaign predicates are evaluated per replica as that replica's artifacts are structurally validated: replicas 1 and 2 before derivation, replica 3 only after the frozen-document SHA-256 exists and before any holdout predicate. A replica-3 campaign failure is a campaign failure that creates no successful bundle; it cannot alter the already-hashed frozen bytes. The report's campaign rows are the conjunction over all three replicas.

A vacuous H3 holdout is a failure: A4-H3-HOLDOUT-PREDICTION fails unless replica 3 exercises every registered H3 input region; the absolute T3 growth to 16,480 pages is scheduled precisely so that the holdout exposes a type-1 conversion with active and inactive slots on both sides of the 16,352-bit boundary.

resolutions.topic: H2 role assignment binds locator ordinal
resolutions.decision: The H2 owned/available ordinals name H1 locator ordinals (first and second hole in ascending offset order), which are replica-invariant in the H1 model; swapping which located row is owned in one replica changes only the canonical H2 model and is A4-H2-REPLICA-DISAGREEMENT.

The transcript schema fixes, per registry position, either a non-null first failure equal to the row's predicate id (39 rows) or, for A4-H1-LOCATOR-PAIR-MULTIPLE only, a null first failure with a mandatory unreachable_assertion (enumeration argument, max measured count 1, and the fixture ids that evaluated the predicate).

No synthetic campaign is required to reach 600,000,000 work units and no charge-injection hook exists in the production analyzer. The work counter comparator is a pure function unit-tested at exactly 600,000,000 (accept) and 600,000,001 (reject); the transcript records that unit-test result as work_counter_comparator_equality. The byte-level A4-RESOURCE-BOUND fixture is the changed-hash one-over campaign. The dispatch-gate transcript additionally requires the production analyzer and independent-validator commits and an additive provenance entry, which the reference harness correctly did not claim.
